samples.summary: `checkControlInventory` still runs only against `?surface=doc`, so nothing verifies that `dom.controls` returns usable, `getByRole`-resolvable names on the new slides toolbar — which is the one thing the slide-author charter's whole strategy rests on.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:798 pins the inventory check to `?surface=doc`, and its comment at :850 records that the accessible-name computation was wrong precisely for MENU ITEMS carrying a shortcut span (`Heading 2⌘+⌥2`) — a shape the slides toolbar has far more of (`Arrange` menu at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/arrange-menu.tsx, border/shape/table pickers). The new persona (scripts/agent/charters-ui/slide-author.md) instructs the explorer to read `dom.controls` and click the names it returns, and states measured counts (9 idle / 13 selected) that no lane pins. `checkSlidesTargeting` (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:488) never touches `dom.controls`, and the slides toolbar is additionally rendered behind `Suspense fallback={null}` (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:569) whose chunk load is not gated by `data-hunt-harness-ready`, so a toolbar that has not arrived yet is indistinguishable from a surface with no controls.

samples.summary: The `dom-invariant` oracle's fire/quiet cases are all driven on `?surface=doc`; the slides persona enables that oracle against a much larger Radix-based toolbar whose duplicate-id / dangling-aria behaviour has never been observed quiet.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:1344 navigates every oracle case to `?surface=doc`, and the `expect === null` branch (:1358-1360) is the only proof that a clean page fires nothing. `scripts/agent/charters-ui/personas.json` gives `slide-author` the `dom-invariant` oracle, so the scan at packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-oracles.mjs:43 (whole-document duplicate-id and dangling `aria-labelledby`/`aria-controls` walk) now runs after every action on a page mounting the full slides toolbar (dropdowns, pickers, table controls). If any of that chrome emits a repeated id or an `aria-controls` pointing at portal content that is not mounted, the oracle fires on every action and the new persona's findings are manufactured by the harness — the exact failure mode the doc-surface quiet case exists to exclude.

samples.summary: `docs/design/hunter-usage.md` still documents the old contract: "Two personas" and "The `slides` surface ... has no persona yet", both falsified by this change.
samples.evidence: docs/design/hunter-usage.md:98 says "Two personas, each with two briefs:" with a table listing only `doc-writer` and `sheet-author`, and :105-109 state "The `slides` surface mounts and answers readers, but **has no persona yet**, so nothing hunts it. `--surface slides` on its own therefore explores nothing". This PR adds `slide-author` with `surface: slides` (scripts/agent/charters-ui/personas.json), so a reader following this page will believe the surface is unhunted and that `--surface slides` selects nothing. Nested-doc link checking would not catch this and prose is not checked at all; the fix belongs in this doc.

samples.summary: The MCP tool schema's click-by-reader example hardcodes `sheet.cellCenter` for every surface, so a slides run is shown an example reader that `checkSurfaceScope` will refuse.
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/hunt-ui-tool.mjs:507 describes `target.reader` as 'A reader returning {x,y}, e.g. "sheet.cellCenter" — this is how you click a canvas cell.' This string is surface-independent while everything around it was made surface-scoped (`describeReaders(surface)` at :532, `z.enum([surface])` at :549). On a `slides` run the only valid point reader is `slides.elementCenter`, and using the advertised one is rejected by `checkSurfaceScope` (:171-183) as belonging to another surface — a wasted action on a persona whose action budget is 50. The doc/sheet runs are equally shown a reader that does not exist on `doc`. Deriving the example from `readersForSurface(surface)` would keep it honest.

samples.summary: `SURFACES` in the harness page is a hand-written copy of the surface vocabulary that cannot import `UI_SURFACES`, so the very drift this change set out to eliminate now lives here instead.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:70 declares `const SURFACES: readonly HuntSurface[] = ["sheet", "doc", "slides"]`, and bridge.ts:38 restates the same three as a union type. Both are outside anything `scripts/agent/hunt-ui-surfaces.mjs` reaches, and no test cross-checks them against `UI_SURFACES` (`scripts/agent/hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs:73` parses bridge.ts for reader NAMES only, not for `HuntSurface`). A future surface added to `UI_SURFACES` but not here is silently coerced to `sheet` by :75 — the exact substitution the diff's own commentary describes as the failure being retired. `assertMountedSurface` would make it loud at run time, so the impact is bounded, but the copy is unpinned; a parse-based assertion in hunt-ui-surfaces.test.mjs would close it.

verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — `checkControlInventory` navigates only to `?surface=doc` (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:798) and a repo-wide grep for `domControls`/`dom.controls` finds no invocation against `?surface=slides` anywhere (only verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:807/861/922 on doc, plus the agent dispatch at hunt-ui-runner.mjs:192). But under the blast-radius rubric this is not a blocking defect: it names no broken or bypassing call site. No exported symbol changed contract, no guard is bypassed, no caller is left inconsistent; the claim is that a verification lane's coverage does not extend to a new surface, which is exactly the test-adequacy lane this reviewer is told to defer. The concrete failure mode it speculates about is also already guarded generically: `domControls` is surface-agnostic and joins content at element boundaries specifically for the `Heading 2 ⌘+⌥2` shape (hunt-ui-dom.mjs:63-86), and verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:850-877 opens a real menu and asserts every `menuitem*` name resolves through `getByRole` against that identical DOM shape — the slides `Arrange` items render the same text-node-plus-`Shortcut`-span structure (arrange-menu.tsx:79-86, 186-190), and no unresolvable slides name is demonstrated. The `Suspense fallback={null}` sub-claim is likewise not a broken consumer: both the driver (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:234) and the oracle lane (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:490-491) navigate with `waitUntil: "networkidle"` before waiting on `READY_SELECTOR`, and reasoning about the new readiness effect itself is inside-the-diff correctness, not blast radius.
